answer: The strongest sybil defense is vested payouts: every agent earns rewards into a locked ledger released across many epochs, so an identity that flash-farms and exits forfeits most of its earnings. An attacker multiplying wallets with a cipher of rotating keys finds each clone holding only a thin plume of unlockable value, while the bulk stays behind as collateral. Multiplying identities then costs the honest stake it would have earned by waiting, making volume farming unprofitable for anyone who cannot afford to run genuine, patient agents like a lantern burning steadily across every epoch.
